prompt: a top-down open-world city driving game at night. Neon streets, rain reflections, traffic, a few ramps and police lights in the distance. I drive a car around freely, drift around corners and hit a ramp for a jump. Original art and setting only - no references to any existing game. It must look great in a vertical screen recording: bold colours, big readable UI, a speedometer and a "DRIFT x2" combo counter that pops on screen.
change_request_1d:
Make these changes for a video recording:
1. Add a cinematic camera that follows the car slightly behind and above.
2. Make drift smoke, sparks and the ramp jump more dramatic.
3. Add an on-screen title card at start: "MY OPEN WORLD - BUILT BY CLAUDE".
4. Add a toggle (key H) that hides all UI except the speedometer.
Keep everything else the same.

questions.asked: How should it feel: tight and arcade, grippy until you drift (usual); heavy and grounded, with weight and early braking; or kart, tiny turns and hops into drifts?
questions.answer: Fast, arcadey, satisfying drifts. Not a simulator.

questions.asked: How should it look: the view from above that follows the car, a tilted 3D top-down (usual, as you said top-down); and a direction: saturated 90s arcade neon (usual) or isometric stylised low poly? Paste a screenshot or two, or drop them in references/.
questions.answer: Neon night city, rain, glowing signs, chunky low-poly / blocky style

questions.asked: How hard: when should trouble first come and what does a crash cost? Usual: easy to drive in the first minute, a real challenge in the rooftop climb; a crash costs a few seconds, one key puts you back on the road.
questions.answer: Easy to drive in the first 10 seconds

questions.asked: The goal: free roam with a list of things to try (usual), or a set challenge on top, like reaching a landmark against the clock?
questions.answer: Free roam plus a short 'reach the rooftop ramp' challenge

questions.asked: Pickups: none, pure driving (usual), or boost earned by sliding and near misses?
A slice of the game: a short session from start to finish (usual), or a quick test of one mechanic, like how the drift feels?

genres_matched: action-adventure (open world: one open place with a landmark)
